metadata.title: Tsugumi — kintsugi design, and the studio to make it
metadata.description: From a photo of a broken piece, Tsugumi shows it restored in gold, then finds a studio, an estimated cost and how long it will take.

brand.name: Tsugumi
brand.aiMockTitle: The AI agents are not connected yet. Analysis, design options and copy are mock responses.

landing.lead: Send us a photo of the broken piece and the memory attached to it. We show you how it could look reborn in gold, then hand you a studio that can do it — with return shipping, an estimated total and a finish date.

how.step1Body: One picture of the cracked or chipped piece you can't bring yourself to throw away.
how.step2Body: Your own piece, shown whole again with gold seams following the real breaks.
how.step3Body: Compare fit, price and turnaround, and we connect you to someone who can take it on.

kintsugi.label: What is Kintsugi
kintsugi.title: The break becomes the view.
kintsugi.photoPlaceholder: photo: kintsugi bowl detail, gold seams
kintsugi.body1: Kintsugi is the Japanese craft of joining a broken vessel with lacquer and dusting the seam with gold. Rather than hiding the damage, it keeps it as part of the time the piece has lived through.
kintsugi.body2: It belongs to the same thinking as wabi-sabi — finding worth in what is chipped and worn. Tsugumi connects your piece to the studios that carry on that craft.
